name: reach.verdict.C-PERC.trend/trend/useless
measured_on: MADE-UP DATA, not a plant result: C-PERC.trend trend, useless input (Gap_B = 0 for V1 and the primary variant): the rule should give loss

extra.label: inconclusive
extra.why: a loss needs the Gap_B intervals of V1 and of the primary variant inside +-0.03. The trend stratum has few checkpoints an episode and the closed-loop coverage of B3 has sd 0.196 on dev, so the per-seed difference has sd 0.22; at n = 500 and level 0.05 / 18 the spread-scaled half-width is 0.1765 x s = 0.039, beyond 0.03 even for a gap of exactly 0 (it would need s at most 0.170). The pooled stratum (s = 0.11, half-width 0.019) does reach it

name: reach.verdict.C-PLAN.P0/cost/perfect
measured_on: MADE-UP DATA, not a plant result: C-PLAN.P0 cost, perfect input (P0 at the cheapest honest plan (2 units), no failures either side): the rule should give win

extra.label: inconclusive
extra.why: the cost margin is 0.02 of the cap (4 units). B3, now that it no longer stalls (0003 A17, A18), costs 5.33 units on dev, sd 0.89, so a planner can save at most 3.33 units even if it costs only 2 (two planned jobs, nothing else), while a win needs more than 4 units plus the half-width: 4.19 on the spread-scaled bound (0.216 x 0.89 = 0.19 units). The planner's own cost on dev is 4.16 units, so its saving is 1.17, and its cost has a tail (2 of 40 episodes fail; the paired difference has sample kurtosis 14.9 against the guard's limit of 6 at n = 300), which sends the bound to the betting sequence: 16 units whatever the data, so 20 units are needed
